name: @tocharianou/grafana-mcp

tools.name: execute_grafana_api
tools.description:
Execute any Grafana HTTP API endpoint directly. Use this for all operations not covered by dedicated tools.

Common API paths:
  Dashboards  : GET  /api/dashboards/uid/:uid  |  DELETE /api/dashboards/uid/:uid
  Folders     : GET  /api/folders  |  POST /api/folders  |  DELETE /api/folders/:uid
  Datasources : GET  /api/datasources  |  POST /api/datasources  |  DELETE /api/datasources/uid/:uid
  Annotations : GET  /api/annotations  |  POST /api/annotations  |  PATCH /api/annotations/:id
  Alerting    : GET  /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules  |  POST /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules
  Contact pts : GET  /api/v1/provisioning/contact-points
  Policies    : GET  /api/v1/provisioning/policies
  Admin/org   : GET  /api/health  |  GET /api/org  |  GET /api/org/users
  Service accs: GET  /api/serviceaccounts/search  |  POST /api/serviceaccounts
  Permissions : GET  /api/dashboards/uid/:uid/permissions  |  POST /api/folders/:uid/permissions
  Plugins     : GET  /api/plugins  |  GET /api/plugins/:id/settings
  Provisioning: POST /api/admin/provisioning/:type/reload
  Library     : GET  /api/library-elements
  Teams       : GET  /api/teams/search
  Playlists   : GET  /api/playlists

Full API reference: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developers/http_api/

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits for large responses. Use sparingly.

tools.name: search_dashboards
tools.description: Search Grafana for dashboards and folders by title, tag, or folder. This is the primary entry point for any Grafana investigation — use it first to discover relevant dashboards. For large result sets the tool automatically switches to a smart summary view to save context tokens, similar to how the Elasticsearch MCP handles large index sets. Use summary_mode to control the level of detail.

query.description: Search query to match against dashboard/folder titles

tag.description: Filter by one or more tags (all must match)

type.description: 'dash-db' for dashboards only, 'dash-folder' for folders only

folderUids.description: Restrict search to specific folder UIDs

summary_mode.description: Return a grouped summary instead of full list. Auto-enabled for >50 results.

summary_level.description: Summary detail: auto (intelligent by size), full (all folders), compact (top folders), minimal (counts only)

break_token_rule.description: Bypass token limits for large result sets.

tools.name: get_dashboard_summary
tools.description: Get a compact, token-efficient overview of a Grafana dashboard: title, tags, panel count, panel list (id, title, type, query count), template variables, and time range. Use this before get_dashboard_panel_queries or run_panel_query to understand the dashboard structure without fetching its full JSON.

uid.description: The UID of the dashboard to summarize

tools.name: get_dashboard_panel_queries
tools.description: Extract the raw query expressions from every panel in a Grafana dashboard (or a specific panel). Returns panel id, title, datasource uid/type, refId, and the query string. Optionally apply variable overrides to see the final substituted query (processedQuery). Use this after get_dashboard_summary to preview panel queries before executing them with run_panel_query.

panelId.description: Filter to a single panel by numeric ID

tools.name: run_panel_query
tools.description: Execute the live data query for one or more Grafana dashboard panels. Automatically fetches the dashboard, extracts queries from the specified panels, substitutes template variables and Grafana temporal macros ($__range, $__interval, $__rate_interval), then posts to /api/ds/query. Supports all datasource types (Prometheus, Loki, ClickHouse, CloudWatch, etc.). Returns raw data frame results keyed by panel ID. Use get_dashboard_summary to find panel IDs.

panelIds.description: One or more numeric panel IDs

queryIndex.description: Zero-based index of the query within each panel's targets (default: 0)

start.description: Start time: relative ('now-1h', 'now-6h'), RFC3339, or Unix ms

end.description: End time: 'now', RFC3339, or Unix ms

break_token_rule.description: Bypass token limits for large results.

tools.name: query_prometheus
tools.description: Execute an instant PromQL query against a Prometheus datasource via Grafana's proxy. Returns the current metric value at a point in time. Use for checking current state (e.g. 'up', 'rate(http_requests_total[5m])'). Get the datasource UID from list_datasources (via execute_grafana_api GET /api/datasources) or get_dashboard_panel_queries.

time.description: Evaluation time as RFC3339 or Unix seconds (default: now)

break_token_rule.description: Bypass token limits for large results.

tools.name: query_prometheus_range
tools.description: Execute a range PromQL query against a Prometheus datasource via Grafana's proxy. Returns time-series values over a window. Use for trend analysis and graphing. Step controls resolution (e.g. '15s', '1m', '5m').

start.description: Start time — RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z') or Unix seconds

end.description: End time — RFC3339 or Unix seconds

break_token_rule.description: Bypass token limits for large results.

tools.name: list_prometheus_metric_names
tools.description: List all available metric names in a Prometheus datasource. Use this to discover what metrics exist before writing PromQL queries. Optionally filter with a regex pattern.

break_token_rule.description: Bypass token limits for large results.

tools.name: query_loki_logs
tools.description:
Execute a LogQL query against a Loki datasource via Grafana's proxy.

Supports both log stream queries and metric queries:
  Log stream : {app="nginx"} |= "error"
  Metric     : rate({app="nginx"}[5m])
  With parser: {namespace="prod"} | json | level="error"

queryType:
  'range'   — time series over the window (default, returns log lines or metric values)
  'instant' — single evaluation at end time (useful for current metric value)

Times are passed as RFC3339 strings; the tool handles nanosecond conversion internally.
Get the datasource UID from execute_grafana_api GET /api/datasources or list_loki_label_names.

start.description: Start time as RFC3339 (default: 1 hour ago)

limit.description: Max log lines for stream queries (default: 100, max: 5000)

step.description: Step in seconds for metric range queries (e.g. 60)

break_token_rule.description: Bypass token limits for large results.

tools.name: list_loki_label_names
tools.description: List all label names (keys) available in a Loki datasource within the given time range. Returns an array like ['app', 'env', 'pod', 'namespace']. Use this to discover what labels exist before writing LogQL stream selectors.

start.description: Start time as RFC3339 (default: 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_loki_label_values
tools.description: Retrieve all unique values for a specific Loki label name. For example, querying 'env' might return ['prod', 'staging', 'dev']. Use list_loki_label_names first to discover available label names.

labelName.description: Label name to retrieve values for (e.g. 'app', 'namespace', 'pod')

start.description: Start time as RFC3339 (default: 1 hour ago)
